issues.display_title: Issue #974: Handle Issue Can't Link an Event to a Place
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT

Root cause. Points were an explicit non-goal of the Event Place tab
(PRD §2): only areas and shapes carrying Information were listed, so a pin — a
kiosk, a stage, a stall — could never host an event. On top of that the
dispatch in handleEventPlace was binary: a point place went out as "shape"
and selected nothing.

Fix. The place set now includes points. Two kinds of pin stay out on
purpose:

  • a hidden pin (#278) draws no visitor marker, so its Place button would fly
    to nothing — the same reasoning that keeps legacy lift/stairs areas out (#769);
  • a pano-linked pin is a tour node minted by Add Panorama, one per imported
    panorama; listing them would bury the real places under hundreds of rows.

Everything downstream already handled points (the preview Selection union, the
fly-to anchor lookup, the info card's point branch, the event badge keyed by
object id), so only the place list and the dispatch changed. Point ids are also
more durable than detected-room ids: levelToModel/modelToLevel pass points
through by identity.

Files

  • src/lib/events/places.ts — points in the place set, hidden/pano-linked excluded
  • src/components/editor/event-modal/PlaceTab.tsx
  • src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx — point branch in the place dispatch
  • src/store/useMapStore.types.ts
  • src/lib/events/__tests__/places.test.ts

issues.display_title: Issue #975: Fix Low Contrast and Illegible Text on Map Overlay Dropdown Buttons
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

The dropdown buttons on the right side of the map top bar ("Default" map style and "Level 2" floor selector) currently use white text and icons over a semi-transparent light background. When displayed over light map layers, the text becomes completely illegible due to poor color contrast.

Square One Mall V6 (Demo)
MapThru: https://map-thru.com/v/UkZnTKwv
Mappedin: https://sq1district.com/mall-map#/?tab=popular
Google: https://maps.app.goo.gl/jDfEuLZP2Y6P38Kc9

RESULT

Demo by Developer

video-975-dropdown-contrast.mp4

Root cause — not the text colour: a cascade collision. BuildingSelector / FloorSelector ask for their own chrome surface with bg-(--editor-canvas-white), but SelectTrigger's base class list (src/components/ui/select.tsx:44) carries dark:bg-input/30 dark:hover:bg-input/50. A dark: variant outranks the unprefixed utility beside it, so in the dark theme both pickers painted a 3%-alpha pill under near-white text — legible over the editor's dark chrome, invisible over a light basemap on /v/{key}.

Measured in the dark theme, before:

control computed background
Search Area button lab(3.6999 0 0) — opaque
Building / Floor dropdown oklab(0.99… / 0.03) — see-through

Fix — restate the pair with the dark: prefix in both selectors so tailwind-merge drops the base one. Both controls now paint the same surface the Search / Direction / Event buttons already do, in either theme. ui/select.tsx is untouched: its translucent default is right for the forms that use it.

Who was affected — Providers sets defaultTheme="light" enableSystem, so a dark OS alone is not enough. Probed: theme=dark stored → affected; theme=system + dark OS → affected; dark OS with nothing stored → light, unaffected. In practice: anyone who used the app's theme toggle on that origin (an owner opening their own share link, as reported here).

Verification — before/after filmed at 60 fps on the published share link; the scenario asserts the dropdown's computed background differs from the button's on development and is identical on the fix, so the take fails if this regresses. pnpm test 239 files / 2294 passed, pnpm lint and tsc --noEmit clean.

Files: src/components/editor/BuildingSelector.tsx, src/components/editor/FloorSelector.tsx

issues.display_title: Issue #976: The blue line panorama link changes to a plain link without a period when in overview mode
issues.main_description_html:
WhatsApp.Video.2026-09-09.at.3.35.19.PM.mp4

RESULT

Root cause. Pelee Island Blue Line (Demo) (/v/H2s94H3V) is a panorama route: 4,696 points and 4,671 panoLinks on one level, with no walls, areas or Building records. Zooming out past 16.25 switches the viewer to Overview, which draws building massing and hides everything indoor (#563 / PRD R25). This project has no massing, so the whole route vanished (label canvas 1,953 px → 0 px) and the toolbar dropped to Search Area. With no Building record there was no dropdown to get back; only zooming in restored it.

Fix.

  1. Overview only engages when a level has wall/area geometry (levelBBox, the test the massing builder itself uses). Projects with buildings behave exactly as before.
  2. Keeping the route on screen at island scale mounted all 4,696 dot buttons and pan dropped to ~2 fps (583 ms median frame, 83 long tasks). So past the Overview threshold the route is drawn as its connection line only, with point markers dropped by the existing site-scale filter. Connection lines are converted to Mercator and joined into polylines once per connection set (chainSegments, since panoLinks are unordered). Sub-pixel vertices are skipped inside a polyline without opening gaps.

Result. Island-view pan at 16.7 ms median / 0 long tasks (GPU Chrome). On the recording rig at steady state: 8.0 / 11.5 ms, versus 12.4 / 17.6 ms for development at close zoom. The close view on the route paints the same pixels as development (2,546 px). pnpm test 2313 passed, lint and tsc clean.

Files: src/lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts, src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx, src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts, src/lib/map/panoConnections.ts (+ useAutoOutdoor.test.tsx, panoConnections.test.ts)

issues.display_title: Issue #977: Resolve the issue where you cannot zoom out completely or zoom out at all, even though “Fit to Plan” allows you to view the entire image.
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

videos/video-dd643aa4-74b0-42df-8afe-c5b4ec6b228c.mp4

RESULT

Demo by Developer

video-977-zoom-out-floor.mp4

Root cause. fit2D (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/view.ts) sets ctx.sc
straight from the plan bounds and clamps nothing, while zoomAt floored every
step at a fixed ZOOM_MIN = 0.1. On a plan large enough to fit below 0.1 —
a tour-scale project whose points span a whole site, like Pelee Island Blue
Line — that floor sat above the view Fit to Plan produces:

  • the first wheel-out is clamped up to 0.1, which is a ~5x zoom in — the plan leaves the screen entirely
  • every notch after that is ns === ctx.sc → early return, nothing happens
  • only the Fit to Plan button can get the view back
  • the same clamp broke zoom-in down there, snapping 0.06 straight to 0.1

Measured notch by notch (.playwright-mcp/demo/977/probe-notches.mjs, 1920x1080,
plan canvas 811x1008, on a scratch copy of the reported project):

build view stops moving at
development notch 2
fixed notch 9 — the new floor, a quarter of the fitted scale

Fix. The zoom floor now tracks the fit scale instead of being a constant,
with ZOOM_FIT_MARGIN (4x) of pull-back past Fit so the page can still be
viewed with margin. fit2D and the floor share one scaleToFit helper so the
two cannot disagree about where Fit sits. The bounds walk only runs when the
floor is actually in play, so an ordinary wheel step costs nothing extra.

An ordinary plan fits well above 0.1 and keeps exactly the floor it had today —
no behaviour change there.

Acceptance

  • From Fit to Plan, the wheel zooms out further instead of freezing
  • Repeated wheel-out keeps reducing the scale (notch 2 → notch 9)
  • Zoom-in below 0.1 steps smoothly instead of snapping to 0.1
  • The toolbar's Zoom out button follows the same floor
  • Ordinary floor plans keep the existing 0.1 floor
  • A collapsed plan panel (0x0 canvas) cannot produce a negative floor

Files

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/view.ts — scaleToFit + fitScale, floor in zoomAt
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/constants.ts — ZOOM_FIT_MARGIN
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/zoom-floor.test.ts — 6 cases (3 fail on the old fixed floor, verified)

pnpm test 2300 passed · pnpm lint 0 errors · tsc --noEmit clean

Demo. .playwright-mcp/demo/977/video-977-zoom-out-floor.mp4 — real
before/after, 1920x1080 60 fps on the GPU, :6062 (development) against
:6060 (this branch), same project and same Fit. Filmed on a scratch copy of
the reported project, deleted afterwards.

issues.display_title: Issue #978: Handle Issue The position of the panorama link changes when a wall or other object is added
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

WhatsApp.Video.2026-09-09.at.3.46.03.PM.mp4

RESULT

Demo by Developer

video-978-coord-space-freeze.mp4

Root cause. A floor imported from a tour is thousands of pano pins and no
walls or areas at all. levelBBox (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts) measures
walls and areas only, so computeBBox is null for that document and
computeCoordSpace falls back to its placeholder space — which every pin, and
every pano link drawn between them, is nonetheless projected through.

Draw the first wall and the box stops being null, so the derived space jumps to
the centre and scale of that one wall. Measured on the reported project:

cxPx cyPx mpp
before the first wall 0 0 0.1
after one small wall 180 180 0.3125

Re-anchored and 3.1x rescaled. Nothing about the pins changed — they are
re-projected through a different space, which is the whole network sliding off
the coastline in the recording.

Read straight off the reported project (c201d5e3, read-only via
/v1/floorplan, the editor was never opened on it — it autosaves):

coordSpace       : null
project frame    : {} placed: false
buildings placed : false      levels placed: false
panoLinks        : 4671
level o0AgXs5…   : walls=4 areas=1 points=4696

Those 4 walls and 1 area are the square drawn in the recording — the project is
sitting in the shifted state now.

Why the existing guard missed it. freezeCoordSpace (#778) exists to stop
exactly this, and refused on both of its gates: computeBBox is null so it
"could not measure" the document, and the project is unplaced. This project is
both. Placement is what makes a measurable project's space load-bearing; pins
are what make an unmeasurable one's. The guard now asks whichever question
fits the document in front of it.

What was deliberately not changed. The derivation. Making levelBBox
measure pins would re-anchor every project that has no stamp today — including
this one, whose 4,696 pins would be rescaled to a 50 m footprint on load. The
stamp is output-preserving by construction: it stores the value
computeCoordSpace was about to return anyway.

Stamped at load, beside the placement pins it is the sibling of, on both
load paths (the /v1/floorplan blob and the canvas_data column) — fixing one
only would fix the bug on one of the two.

Recovering this project. A floor already broken by a stray wall is
deliberately left unstamped (measurable but unplaced), so the existing route
still works: delete the 4 walls and 1 area added during the recording and the
pins return to where they were. The next load then stamps the floor and it
cannot break again. Locked in by a test so a later change cannot quietly cement
the damaged state.

Acceptance

  • Adding a wall to a tour-only floor no longer moves its pins or pano links
  • Works on an unplaced project — the reported project has no transform
  • The stamp equals what was already being rendered (nothing moves on load)
  • A genuinely empty project stays free to re-fit, placed or not
  • A measurable project keeps the pre-existing placed/unplaced rule (#778)
  • An already-broken floor stays recoverable by deleting the stray wall
  • Both load paths stamp

Files

  • src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts — freezeCoordSpace gates + drawsThroughCoordSpace
  • src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts — stamp on the floorplan-blob load
  • src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts — stamp on the canvas_data load
  • src/lib/map/__tests__/coordspace-tour-only.test.ts — 7 cases
  • src/lib/persistence/__tests__/wizardState.test.ts — 2 cases at the load call site

pnpm test 2309 passed · pnpm lint 0 errors · tsc --noEmit clean

Demo. .playwright-mcp/demo/978/video-978-coord-space-freeze.mp4 — real
before/after, 1920x1080 60 fps on the GPU, :6062 (development) against :6060
(this branch). Two scratch copies of the reported project, both stripped back to
the state the bug is reported from (4,696 pins, 4,671 links, 0 walls), then
deleted. Each half draws the same closed rectangle the reporter drew and compares
the map before/after from one pinned camera (the editor map re-fits once
walls exist, so an unpinned comparison would measure the camera):

build SSIM before vs after what is on screen
development 0.953 the whole link network collapses into a blob off the roads
fixed 0.992 network on the same roads; only the new room marker differs

The baseline worktree differs from development only by 3c56644 (hover
highlight, #981) — nothing in the coord-space or pano-link path.

issues.display_title: Issue #981: perf(map): pan drops to ~1 fps and hover highlight lags on large floor plans
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported from a screen recording (samples/superlag.mp4): on Map view, preview and live, panning the map collapses to ~1 fps once the view drops from the outdoor massing into the real indoor model, and hovering a room lights it up noticeably after the cursor. Reproduced on the Square One demo (/v/UkZnTKwv, 684 areas / 6,824 walls across two levels).

Both turned out to be the same trigger — MapLibre fires styledata for any paint, filter or layout write, and the indoor hover highlight fires one per mousemove.

Root cause

1. The whole model GeoJSON was rebuilt mid-pan. Two paths ran canvasDataToGeoJson / outdoorGeoJson on every hover change: the styledata handler in useFloorPlanLayer / useOutdoorLayer (meant only to restore layers after a base-style swap), and the push effect, which was keyed on the caller's { lat, lng } object literal — a fresh object on every re-render. CPU profile over a 12-move drag: 5.9 s of 14.2 s wall clock inside closedWallOwners alone (O(walls × closed rooms × ring vertices), uncached), two full rebuilds per frame.

2. The hover highlight took a React round-trip. The handler only called setHovered; the filter was written later from a useEffect, so the highlight landed a frame after the cursor and painted on the frame after that. Worse, the same styledata handler re-applied hover/selection from refs the handler had not updated yet, flipping the highlight back to the previous room until React caught up.

Scope

  • useFloorPlanLayer — styledata handler becomes restore-only (runs only when the source or the mode's sentinel layer is actually gone); export applyHighlight.
  • useOutdoorMode (useOutdoorLayer) — build the massing once per input change, push it once; styledata re-adds only after a real style swap.
  • useFloorPlanLayer / useFloorPlanLabels / useOutdoorLayer — key effects on lat/lng values instead of the { lat, lng } object identity, so no caller can retrigger them by re-rendering.
  • usePreviewSelectionLayers + Editor3DMapView + PreviewOverlay — paint the highlight in the hover event itself (both writers: the area-extrusion handler and the marker-pill hover, which is where most hovers on a dense floor come from). The effect still runs afterwards and MapLibre discards the identical filter.

Acceptance criteria

  • Panning indoors on Square One holds a normal frame rate; no canvasDataToGeoJson / closedWallOwners in a pan profile.
  • Hovering a room applies the highlight in the same event as the pointer, and it never flips back to the previously hovered room.
  • A base-style swap (vector ↔ satellite) still restores the floor plan and the outdoor massing.
  • Map view, preview, live /v/[key] and embed all behave the same.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Measured (real GPU, 1440×900, /v/UkZnTKwv)

before after
closedWallOwners per 40-step drag 2,875 ms 0 ms
drag wall clock 28.5 s 9.6 s
p90 frame during pan 300 ms 133 ms
hover → highlight applied 60 ms 1 ms
hover → highlight painted 82 ms (2 frames) 24 ms (1 frame)

Demo (before vs after, side by side with a live HUD): .playwright-mcp/demo/map-pan-hover-lag/video-map-pan-hover-lag.mp4

RESULT

Root cause was one trigger with two symptoms: MapLibre fires styledata for any paint/filter/layout write, and the indoor hover highlight fires one per mousemove.

  • styledata handlers in useFloorPlanLayer / useOutdoorLayer are restore-only now — they rebuild and re-apply visibility/hover/selection only when the source or the mode's sentinel layer is actually gone. That killed both the mid-pan re-tessellation and the flip-back that pushed a stale hover over the current one.
  • useFloorPlanLayer / useFloorPlanLabels / useOutdoorLayer key their effects on lat/lng values instead of the caller's { lat, lng } object identity.
  • The hover handlers (usePreviewSelectionLayers, Editor3DMapView, and the marker-pill hover in PreviewOverlay / Editor3DMapView) call applyHighlight in the event that decided the hover; the effect still runs and MapLibre discards the identical filter.

Tests: src/lib/map/__tests__/useFloorPlanLayer.rebuild.test.tsx + useOutdoorLayer.rebuild.test.tsx, 11 cases, five of which fail on the pre-fix code. pnpm test 239 files / 2294 tests green, pnpm lint 0 errors, tsc --noEmit clean.

Measured on a real GPU at 1440x900 against /v/UkZnTKwv: closedWallOwners 2,875 ms -> 0 ms per 40-step drag, drag wall clock 28.5 s -> 9.6 s, p90 frame 300 ms -> 133 ms, hover -> highlight applied 60 ms -> 1 ms and painted 82 ms (2 frames) -> 24 ms (1 frame).
